title: AI Will Replace Software Engineers? Here’s What’s Actually Happening
summary: Tech recruiter contrasts AI CEOs' 'coding is dead' claims with record engineer pay; AI amplifies experts, not novices.

assertions.quote: 90% of all code ask an engineering team at a real company, it's not even close yet

verdicts.note: Industry-wide, AI did not write ~90% of code by late 2025; but some AI-heavy teams (including at Anthropic) reported 70-90%+, so it partly came true in narrow settings.

assertions.quote: If you truly believed AI was about to replace software engineers, would you pay the median one $750,000 a year?

verdicts.note: Levels.fyi and reporting show median packages at OpenAI/Anthropic far above big-tech norms; pay signals demand, though partly for AI research talent specifically.

assertions.quote: For someone with no experience, AI gives you a toy ... for someone with real experience, AI is a rocket strapped to their back

verdicts.note: Experts get more reliable results and catch errors, but several RCTs show larger measured speedups for juniors, and METR found experts slowed; contested.

assertions.quote: AI will replace engineers isn't a prediction, kind of like a pitch deck

verdicts.note: Labs do have incentives and many evals are self-reported, but independent evals (METR, SWE-bench, LMArena) largely confirm capability gains.

assertions.quote: The actual coding was never the real job

verdicts.note: Studies of developer time show coding is a minority of work; DORA and Faros 2025 found individual coding gains often don't translate into delivery throughput.

assertions.quote: go up the stack on purpose. System design, architecture

verdicts.note: Humans still own constraints and tradeoffs, but models can now propose reasonable designs when given context; the gap is narrowing.
